title: Satellite Image Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks for Earth Observation Applications
content: In environmental monitoring satellite images are used along with land use mapping, disaster management, agricultural assessment and climate change analysis. The increasing availability of high-resolution Earth observation data from satellite missions such as Sentinel-2 has created a demand for automated image analysis techniques capable of processing large-scale geospatial datasets efficiently. In this research we use CNN model for satellite image classification using land(use) and land(cover) imagery. We used CNN with three convolutional blocks with 32, 64, and 128 filters followed by ReLU activation, MaxPooling, Dropout regularization, and a dense classification layer. When performed classification on EuroSAT satellite imagery CNN model achieved classification accuracy exceeding 83%. Training convergence analysis showed rapid learning within 10 epochs, while confusion matrix evaluation confirmed robust discrimination across diverse land-use categories.
